# Hindi beginner dialogues

## Dialogue: Meeting someone new in Hindi

<!-- topic: introductions -->

A short Hindi conversation — meeting someone new. Ravi (A) meets Asha (B) at a friend's house in Delhi.

- **A:** नमस्ते। (namaste.) — "Hello."
- **B:** नमस्ते जी। (namaste jee.) — "Hello."
- **A:** आपका नाम क्या है? (aapkaa naam kyaa hai?) — "What is your name?"
- **B:** मेरा नाम आशा है। आपका नाम क्या है? (meraa naam Asha hai. aapkaa naam kyaa hai?) — "My name is Asha. What is your name?"
- **A:** मेरा नाम रवि है। आप कहाँ से हैं? (meraa naam Ravi hai. aap kahaan se hain?) — "My name is Ravi. Where are you from?"
- **B:** मैं जयपुर से हूँ। आपसे मिलकर अच्छा लगा। (main Jaipur se hoon. aapse milkar achchhaa lagaa.) — "I am from Jaipur. Nice to meet you."
- **A:** मुझे भी आपसे मिलकर अच्छा लगा। (mujhe bhee aapse milkar achchhaa lagaa.) — "Nice to meet you too."

## Dialogue: Meeting a friend in Hindi

<!-- topic: everyday-conversation -->

A short Hindi conversation — meeting a friend. Two college friends, Ravi (A) and Amit (B), bump into each other in a market in Lucknow.

- **A:** अरे अमित! कैसे हो? (are Amit! kaise ho?) — "Hey Amit! How are you?"
- **B:** मैं ठीक हूँ। तुम सुनाओ? (main theek hoon. tum sunaao?) — "I am fine. And you? (literally: you tell me)"
- **A:** मैं भी ठीक हूँ। बहुत दिनों बाद मिले! (main bhee theek hoon. bahut dinon baad mile!) — "I am also fine. Long time no see!"
- **B:** हाँ। आजकल क्या कर रहे हो? (haan. aajkal kyaa kar rahe ho?) — "Yes. What are you doing these days?"
- **A:** पढ़ाई कर रहा हूँ। तुमने खाना खाया? (padhaaee kar rahaa hoon. tumne khaanaa khaayaa?) — "I am studying. Have you eaten?"
- **B:** हाँ, खा लिया। चलो, चाय पीते हैं। (haan, khaa liyaa. chalo, chaay peete hain.) — "Yes, I have eaten. Let's have tea."
- **A:** ठीक है, चलो। (theek hai, chalo.) — "Okay, let's go."

## Dialogue: Ordering food in Hindi

<!-- topic: restaurant -->

A short Hindi conversation — ordering food. A waiter (A) takes an order from a customer (B) at a dhaba in Delhi.

- **A:** जी, आप क्या लेंगे? (jee, aap kyaa lenge?) — "Yes, what would you like?"
- **B:** एक प्लेट दाल-चावल दीजिए। (ek plet daal-chaaval deejiye.) — "Please give me one plate of rice and dal."
- **A:** पीने के लिए कुछ? (peene ke lie kuchh?) — "Anything to drink?"
- **B:** एक चाय, बिना चीनी के। (ek chaay, binaa cheenee ke.) — "One tea, without sugar, please."
- **A:** ठीक है। और कुछ? (theek hai. aur kuchh?) — "Okay. Anything else?"
- **B:** थोड़ा पानी दीजिए। क्या दाल तीखी है? (thodaa paani deejiye. kyaa daal teekhee hai?) — "Some water, please. Is the dal spicy?"
- **A:** थोड़ी-सी तीखी है। (thodee-see teekhee hai.) — "It's a little spicy."
- **B:** कोई बात नहीं। खाने के बाद बिल ले आइए। (koee baat nahin. khaane ke baad bil le aaiye.) — "That's fine. Please bring the bill after the meal."

## Dialogue: At the shop in Hindi

<!-- topic: shopping -->

A short Hindi conversation — at the shop. Asha (A) buys mangoes from a fruit seller (B) in a market in Bhopal.

- **A:** भैया, आपके पास आम हैं? (bhaiyaa, aapke paas aam hain?) — "Brother, do you have mangoes?"
- **B:** हाँ जी, हैं। (haan jee, hain.) — "Yes, we have."
- **A:** एक किलो कितने का है? (ek kilo kitne kaa hai?) — "How much does one kilo cost?"
- **B:** सौ रुपये। (sau rupaye.) — "One hundred rupees."
- **A:** यह तो बहुत महँगा है। थोड़ा कम कीजिए। (yah to bahut mahangaa hai. thodaa kam keejiye.) — "That is too expensive. Please reduce the price a little."
- **B:** अच्छा, नब्बे रुपये दे दीजिए। (achchhaa, nabbe rupaye de deejiye.) — "Okay, give me ninety rupees."
- **A:** ठीक है, मैं एक किलो ले लूँगी। (theek hai, main ek kilo le loongee.) — "Fine, I will take one kilo. (Asha uses the feminine ले लूँगी.)"

## Dialogue: Asking for directions in Hindi

<!-- topic: directions -->

A short Hindi conversation — asking for directions. A visitor (A) asks a passer-by (B) for the way in Jaipur.

- **A:** सुनिए, रेलवे स्टेशन कहाँ है? (suniye, relve steshan kahaan hai?) — "Excuse me, where is the railway station?"
- **B:** सीधे जाइए, फिर बाएँ मुड़िए। (seedhe jaaiye, phir baaen mudiye.) — "Go straight, then turn left."
- **A:** क्या वह दूर है? (kyaa vah door hai?) — "Is it far?"
- **B:** नहीं, पास में ही है। पैदल पाँच मिनट लगेंगे। (nahin, paas mein hee hai. paidal paanch minat lagenge.) — "No, it is near. About five minutes on foot."
- **A:** बहुत-बहुत धन्यवाद। (bahut-bahut dhanyavaad.) — "Thank you very much."
- **B:** कोई बात नहीं। (koee baat nahin.) — "You're welcome."

## Dialogue: At college in Hindi

<!-- topic: college -->

A short Hindi conversation — at college. Ravi (A), a senior, meets Asha (B) on her first day at a college in Lucknow.

- **A:** हाय, क्या तुम यहाँ नई हो? (haay, kyaa tum yahaan naee ho?) — "Hi, are you new here? (नई is feminine — he is talking to a girl.)"
- **B:** हाँ, आज मेरा पहला दिन है। (haan, aaj meraa pahlaa din hai.) — "Yes, today is my first day."
- **A:** तुम किस क्लास में हो? (tum kis klaas mein ho?) — "Which class are you in?"
- **B:** मैं फ़र्स्ट ईयर में हूँ। लाइब्रेरी कहाँ है? (main farst eeyar mein hoon. laaibreree kahaan hai?) — "I am in first year. Where is the library?"
- **A:** ऑफ़िस के पीछे है। चलो, मैं दिखाता हूँ। (ofis ke peechhe hai. chalo, main dikhaataa hoon.) — "It is behind the office. Come, I will show you."
- **B:** धन्यवाद! परीक्षा कब है? (dhanyavaad! pareekshaa kab hai?) — "Thank you! When is the exam?"
- **A:** अगले महीने। (agle maheene.) — "Next month."

## Dialogue: On the phone in Hindi

<!-- topic: everyday-conversation -->

A short Hindi conversation — on the phone. Ravi (A) phones his friend Asha (B).

- **A:** हेलो? (helo?) — "Hello?"
- **B:** हेलो, कौन बोल रहा है? (helo, kaun bol rahaa hai?) — "Hello, who is speaking?"
- **A:** मैं रवि बोल रहा हूँ। तुम कहाँ हो? (main Ravi bol rahaa hoon. tum kahaan ho?) — "It's me, Ravi. Where are you?"
- **B:** मैं घर पर हूँ। क्या हुआ? (main ghar par hoon. kyaa huaa?) — "I am at home. What happened?"
- **A:** क्या तुम कल फ़्री हो? (kyaa tum kal free ho?) — "Are you free tomorrow?"
- **B:** हाँ, मैं फ़्री हूँ। (haan, main free hoon.) — "Yes, I am free."
- **A:** तो शाम को मेरे घर आओ। (to shaam ko mere ghar aao.) — "Then come to my house in the evening."
- **B:** ठीक है, मैं आऊँगी। मैं तुम्हें बाद में फ़ोन करूँगी। (theek hai, main aaoongee. main tumhen baad mein fon karoongee.) — "Okay, I will come. I will call you later. (Asha uses the feminine forms.)"

## Dialogue: Asking for help in Hindi

<!-- topic: requests -->

A short Hindi conversation — asking for help. A visitor (A) asks a shopkeeper (B) for help in Delhi.

- **A:** सुनिए, क्या आप मेरी मदद कर सकते हैं? (suniye, kyaa aap meree madad kar sakte hain?) — "Excuse me, can you help me?"
- **B:** हाँ जी, बताइए। (haan jee, bataaiye.) — "Yes, tell me."
- **A:** मैं रास्ता भूल गया हूँ। मुझे यह पता समझ नहीं आ रहा। (main raastaa bhool gayaa hoon. mujhe yah pataa samajh nahin aa rahaa.) — "I am lost. I don't understand this address."
- **B:** दिखाइए। यह तो बाज़ार के पास है। (dikhaaiye. yah to baazaar ke paas hai.) — "Show me. This is near the market."
- **A:** थोड़ा धीरे बोलिए। (thodaa dheere boliye.) — "Please speak slowly."
- **B:** बाज़ार जाइए और वहाँ पूछ लीजिए। पास में ही है। (baazaar jaaiye aur vahaan poochh leejiye. paas mein hee hai.) — "Go to the market and ask there. It is close."
- **A:** बहुत-बहुत शुक्रिया। (bahut-bahut shukriyaa.) — "Thank you so much."

## Dialogue: Taking a bus in Hindi

<!-- topic: travel -->

A short Hindi conversation — taking a bus. A passenger (A) talks to the bus conductor (B) on a city bus in Bhopal.

- **A:** क्या यह बस रेलवे स्टेशन जाती है? (kyaa yah bas relve steshan jaatee hai?) — "Does this bus go to the railway station?"
- **B:** हाँ। कहाँ उतरना है? (haan. kahaan utarnaa hai?) — "Yes. Where do you want to get off?"
- **A:** रेलवे स्टेशन पर। टिकट कितने का है? (relve steshan par. tikat kitne kaa hai?) — "At the railway station. How much is the ticket?"
- **B:** बीस रुपये। (bees rupaye.) — "Twenty rupees."
- **A:** कितना समय लगेगा? (kitnaa samay lagegaa?) — "How long will it take?"
- **B:** लगभग आधा घंटा। (lagbhag aadhaa ghantaa.) — "About half an hour."
- **A:** स्टेशन आए तो मुझे बता दीजिए। (steshan aae to mujhe bataa deejiye.) — "Please tell me when we reach the station."
- **B:** ठीक है, बता दूँगा। (theek hai, bataa doongaa.) — "Okay, I will tell you."

## Dialogue: Talking about your day in Hindi

<!-- topic: daily-routine -->

A short Hindi conversation — talking about your day. Ravi (A) asks his friend Asha (B) about her day. Asha uses feminine verb forms.

- **A:** तुम कितने बजे उठती हो? (tum kitne baje uthtee ho?) — "What time do you wake up?"
- **B:** मैं छह बजे उठती हूँ। (main chhah baje uthtee hoon.) — "I wake up at six o'clock."
- **A:** उसके बाद क्या करती हो? (uske baad kyaa kartee ho?) — "What do you do after that?"
- **B:** नहाती हूँ, नाश्ता करती हूँ और कॉलेज जाती हूँ। (nahaatee hoon, naashtaa kartee hoon aur kolej jaatee hoon.) — "I bathe, eat breakfast and go to college."
- **A:** घर कब आती हो? (ghar kab aatee ho?) — "When do you come home?"
- **B:** शाम को घर आती हूँ और पढ़ाई करती हूँ। (shaam ko ghar aatee hoon aur padhaaee kartee hoon.) — "I come home in the evening and study."
- **A:** और सोती कब हो? (aur sotee kab ho?) — "And when do you sleep?"
- **B:** रात को दस बजे सोती हूँ। (raat ko das baje sotee hoon.) — "I sleep at ten o'clock at night."
